title: He Replaced Himself With a Delivery Robot at 63. Social Security Still Counted the Profit as Earnings.
excerpt: When a 63-year-old sole proprietor bought a sidewalk robot to handle his delivery route and filed for early Social Security, he assumed the profit flowing in...

Quick Read

  • Replacing one's self with a robot does not convert sole proprietorship profit into passive income. The SSA still counts it against the earnings test.

  • In 2026, early Social Security claimers lose $1 in benefits for every $2 earned above $24,480, measured on net Schedule C profit.

  • Genuinely moving business income outside the earnings test requires substantive changes to business structure and the owner's role, not just new equipment.

Picture a 63-year-old who has spent a decade running a one-person delivery service. He files for Social Security early, buys a sidewalk delivery robot to handle his route, and figures the checks that keep landing in his business account are now passive. The robot does the walking. He just watches the dashboard. On a retirement forum recently, a similar owner asked whether replacing his own driving with automation meant his profit would stop counting against the earnings test. The short answer surprised him.

Automation changes how the work gets done, but it does not automatically change how the resulting income is classified. For a sole proprietor, continuing business profit generally remains net earnings from self-employment. The company's legal structure and how the owner is paid can also matter. That distinction is the whole ballgame for anyone claiming Social Security before full retirement age (FRA) while still owning a business.

Why the Earnings Test Cares Who Runs the Business

If you claim Social Security before FRA and keep earning, the Social Security Administration (SSA) applies an earnings test. In 2026, someone under full retirement age for the entire year can earn $24,480 before Social Security withholds $1 in benefits for every $2 earned above the limit. For the self-employed, the relevant number is net earnings after allowable business deductions and depreciation. Benefits withheld are not simply refunded later, but Social Security recalculates the monthly benefit at FRA to account for months in which checks were withheld.

想象一下一位 63 岁的老人，他花了十年时间经营一家单人送货服务。 他很早就申请了社会保障，购买了一个人行道送货机器人来处理他的路线，并认为不断落在他的企业帐户中的支票现在是被动的。 机器人负责行走。 他只是看仪表板。 在最近的一个退休论坛上，一位类似的车主询问，用自动化取代自己的驾驶是否意味着他的利润将不再计入收入测试。 简短的回答让他感到惊讶。

自动化改变了工作的完成方式，但它不会自动改变所得收入的分类方式。 对于独资经营者来说，持续营业利润通常仍然是自营职业的净利润。 公司的法律结构以及所有者的报酬方式也很重要。 对于任何在完全退休年龄（FRA）之前领取社会保障但仍拥有企业的人来说，这种区别是整个游戏的全部内容。

为什么盈利测试关心谁经营企业

如果您在 FRA 之前申请社会保障并保持收入，社会保障管理局 (SSA) 会进行收入测试。 到 2026 年，未达到完全退休年龄的人全年可赚取 24,480 美元，但社会保障每超过限额赚取 2 美元，将扣留 1 美元的福利。 对于个体经营者，相关数字是扣除允许的业务扣除和折旧后的净利润。 扣留的福利金不仅会在以后退还，而且社会保障局还会重新计算 FRA 的每月福利金，以考虑扣留支票的月份。
